summary: The lazy registry direction addresses the main eager import, but the proposal underestimates compatibility and concurrency details. The highest-risk issue is importing WeasyPrint inside the async method while only offloading the render call, which still blocks the event loop on first use.

suggestions.title: Define the lazy package export contract explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `querysource/outputs/writers/__init__.py` currently has no `__all__`. A PEP 562 implementation without an explicit export list makes `from querysource.outputs.writers import *` stop exporting writer classes. Add `__all__`, `__dir__`, and cache resolved attributes in module globals.

suggestions.title: Preserve direct WRITERS lookup compatibility
suggestions.rationale: `WRITERS` is a module-level mutable mapping and callers currently receive callable classes from `WRITERS[format]`; the repository test also mutates it with `monkeypatch.setitem`. Replacing values with strings changes direct consumers. Either provide a resolver-backed mutable mapping or explicitly document this API change and test aliases such as `xls`, `xlsx`, and `plain`.

suggestions.title: Keep known-format import failures distinct from fallback
suggestions.rationale: The current response path catches `KeyError` only for unknown formats, while a failure loading a known writer is not silently converted to JSON. The resolver must preserve that distinction: select the JSON fallback only for a missing key, then let `ImportError` from the selected spec surface unchanged.

suggestions.title: Do not claim the package-level lazy export removes output.py from HTTP startup
suggestions.rationale: `services.py` eagerly imports `handlers`, and `handlers/__init__.py` eagerly imports handlers that import `DataOutput` from `querysource.outputs`. Thus HTTP startup will still load `querysource.outputs.output`; the measurable HTTP invariant should be that `weasyprint` and writer modules are absent, unless handler imports are also redesigned.

suggestions.title: Move the first WeasyPrint import into the worker thread
suggestions.rationale: Importing `weasyprint.HTML` inside `PDFWriter.get_response` still performs the first heavy import on the event-loop thread. Put the import, `HTML(...)` construction, and `write_pdf` call in a synchronous helper passed to `asyncio.to_thread`. Also state clearly that `ReportWriter.render_content` still contains synchronous chart work on the event loop.

suggestions.title: Resolve PDF concurrency before enabling parallel offload
suggestions.rationale: `asyncio.to_thread` permits concurrent PDF renders through the default executor, potentially multiplying WeasyPrint memory use. Use an application- or process-scoped bounded limiter or dedicated executor; avoid an unconfigured module-level `asyncio.Semaphore`, which can bind incorrectly across test event loops. Existing executor/semaphore patterns provide a local precedent.

suggestions.title: Test every public import form in isolated processes
suggestions.rationale: The existing test verifies mutable `WRITERS` override behavior but not lazy package exports. Add subprocess coverage for `querysource.queries.qs` and `querysource.outputs.output` with `weasyprint` absent from `sys.modules`, plus explicit imports from `querysource.outputs.writers`, star-import behavior, direct submodules, and all registry specs.

suggestions.title: Test the actual off-loop boundary and failure propagation
suggestions.rationale: A regression test should monkeypatch a slow PDF import/render and verify another coroutine can make progress while it runs. Separate tests should assert that renderer exceptions propagate through `DataOutput.response` into its existing writer-error handling, and that cancellation does not leave the registry or limiter in a poisoned state.

suggestions.title: Isolate registry-cache state between tests
suggestions.rationale: Successful resolution mutates `WRITERS` by caching classes. Tests that assert initial string specs can become order-dependent after another test resolves a writer. Use fresh module state or restore the complete mapping, and separately verify class overrides remain authoritative after a cached resolution.
